diagnostic_evidence.quote:
for all pairwise distinct 
$y_1,\ldots, y_{\ell}\in\mathcal{O}$ and for all 
$\alpha=(\alpha_i)\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell}\setminus\{0\}$, we have 
\begin{equation*}
  \sum_{i,j=1}^{\ell}\alpha_i\alpha_j\Phi(y_i-y_j)>0.

issues.failure_explanation: For a general hypercube, differences $y_i-y_j$ need not belong to $\mathcal O$, so the displayed definition and the subsequent interpolation matrix can evaluate $\Phi$ where it has not been defined.

failure_location.quote:
Let $\mathcal{O}$ be an open hypercube in $\mathbb{R}^d$, and 
let $\Phi: \mathcal{O}\to \mathbb{R}$ be a radial and 
positive definite function

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\Phi$ on $\mathbb R^d$ (or at least on $\mathcal O-\mathcal O$), or formulate the reproducing kernel directly as a two-variable kernel on $\mathcal O\times\mathcal O$.
issues.overall_effect: The general native-space and interpolation setup in Section 2 is ill-defined as stated, although the later Wendland kernel is defined globally.
issues.title: Kernel is evaluated outside its declared domain
issues.why_classification: A local domain correction makes all later expressions well-defined without changing the method or its guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: The matrix for $(x_m^{(i)}-x_m^{(j)})^2\phi^{(2)}(|x^{(i)}-x^{(j)}|)$ must contain the right-hand term $A_2G_m^2$. The stated final term $G_m^2$ omits the factor $A_2$ and therefore does not represent the diagonal Hessian entries.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the final $G_m^2$ by $A_2G_m^2$ in the formula for $B_{mm}(\pi)$.
issues.overall_effect: The matrix-form implementation computes an incorrect diagonal second-derivative contribution and can therefore evaluate the nonlinear operator incorrectly.
issues.title: Incorrect diagonal second-derivative matrix
issues.why_classification: The intended matrix identity has a direct local correction that preserves the algorithm and all advertised complexity.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition of $H$ has five arguments after including $t$ and $x$, with $\varphi(x)$ preceding the drift and Hessian terms. The matrix formula supplies only the latter two quantities and omits $(v_k^h)_j= v^h(t_k,x^{(j)})$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert $(v_k^h)_j$ as the third argument of $H$ before the two derivative expressions.
issues.overall_effect: The stated matrix-form procedure is undefined for the declared signature of $H$ and, if interpreted positionally, evaluates the wrong nonlinearity. The numerical section says it uses this representation.
issues.title: Matrix representation omits the solution-value argument of H
issues.why_classification: The missing argument has a uniquely determined local insertion and does not require changing the method.

issues.failure_explanation: The maximum argument only yields an error $(\Delta t)_m^{3/2}$, but the proof replaces it by $\delta_m^{3/2}$. Since $\delta_m\le(\Delta t)_m$, this replacement decreases the error and is invalid. After division by $\delta_m$, the available term need not vanish because no lower bound relates individual time steps to $\Delta t$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose the approximate maximizers with an error that is $o(\min_i(t_{i+1}-t_i))$ for each grid, or impose a time-grid regularity condition ensuring $(\Delta t)^{3/2}/\delta_m\to0$.
issues.overall_effect: The viscosity subsolution argument, and similarly the asserted supersolution argument, does not establish the required consistency inequality for arbitrary nonuniform time grids allowed by the theorem.
issues.title: Approximate-maximum error is improperly reduced from the maximal step to the selected step
issues.why_classification: The theorem can retain its scope by a routine refinement of the approximate-maximizer tolerance, without changing the scheme or adding a substantive lemma.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 4.9 controls $v^h$ and its derivatives only on $(-R,R)^d$, whereas Lemma 4.10 requires a uniformly bounded, globally Lipschitz function on all of $\mathbb R^d$. The cited results therefore do not establish that the function used as $u$ satisfies Lemma 4.10's hypothesis.

failure_location.quote:
Further, Assumption \ref{assum:4.1} and Lemma \ref{lem:4.9} 
imply that $F(t,\cdot;v^h(t,\cdot))$ is bounded and Lipschitz continuous. 
This together with Lemma \ref{lem:4.10} guarantees 
$J_m\to 0$ as $m\to\infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the interior derivative bounds to obtain uniformly bounded Lipschitz nodal data and construct a uniformly bounded Lipschitz extension to $\mathbb R^d$; its interpolant agrees with the required one because interpolation depends only on nodal values.
issues.overall_effect: The proof does not justify $J_m\to0$, leaving the interpolation consistency term uncontrolled in the main convergence theorem.
issues.title: Global Lipschitz interpolation estimate is applied using only interior stability
issues.why_classification: A standard bounded Lipschitz extension supplies the missing admissible input locally and preserves the convergence rate and theorem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
let $\varphi$ be a $C^3$-function on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d$ such that 
$\overline{v}-\varphi$ has a global strict maximum at $(t,x)$

issues.failure_explanation: The viscosity test function is arbitrary and is never shown to satisfy the fixed $C_1$ bound required by Lemma 4.11. In particular, its Hessian and third derivatives can exceed the stability constant for $v^h$, so the lemma cannot be invoked as written.

failure_location.quote:
With the representation (\ref{eq:4.5}), we apply Lemma \ref{lem:4.11} for the family 
$\{v^{h_m}(t_{k_m+1},\cdot), \varphi(t_{k_m+1},\cdot)\}_{m\ge 1}$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each fixed test function and a bounded neighborhood of the contact point, enlarge the constant defining $\mathcal D$ and Lemma 4.11 so that it bounds both the approximants and that test function.
issues.overall_effect: The key max-min comparison is not established for all viscosity test functions, so the claimed subsolution and supersolution properties remain incomplete.
issues.title: Max-min lemma is applied to an arbitrary test function outside its bounded-derivative hypothesis
issues.why_classification: The constants in the local argument may depend on the fixed test function, so a short reparameterization repairs the application without weakening the theorem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
$\tilde{u}^{\varepsilon}(x)=u^{\varepsilon}(x)\zeta(x/R)$, where 
$\zeta$ is a $C^{\infty}$-function on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with compact support such that 
 $0\le \zeta\le 1$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, 
$\zeta=1$ on $\{|x|\le 1\}$

issues.failure_explanation: The condition $\zeta(x/R)=1$ is guaranteed only when $|x|\le R$. For $d>1$, the cube $(-R,R)^d$ contains points with $|x|>R$, including possible collocation points. Thus neither $u^\varepsilon=\tilde u^\varepsilon$ at every evaluated $x$ nor $I(u^\varepsilon)=I(\tilde u^\varepsilon)$ follows.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose the cutoff to equal one on a ball containing the whole cube, for example on $\{|x|\le\sqrt d\}$ before scaling, with compact support in a slightly larger ball.
issues.overall_effect: The Sobolev interpolation estimate is applied to a cutoff function that need not agree with the original function where required, leaving Lemma 4.10 and its use in the convergence proof unsupported.
issues.title: Cutoff does not equal one on the interpolation cube
issues.why_classification: Changing the cutoff radius is a short local repair and only alters dimension-dependent constants.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Next, take $\delta_1\in (0,1]$ such that $x+\sqrt{\delta}w\in\mathcal{O}$ for all  
$w\in\mathcal{X}_{\delta,\theta}$, and $\delta\le\delta_1$.

issues.failure_explanation: For points $x$ arbitrarily close to the boundary of an open bounded set, no single positive $\delta_1$ ensures that all shifts $x+\sqrt\delta w$ remain in $\mathcal O$. The appended proof chooses $\delta_1$ only after fixing $x$, contradicting the uniform quantifiers in the statement; otherwise the sampled value of $\varphi$ may be undefined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict $x$ to a compact subset $\mathcal O'\Subset\mathcal O$, with $\delta_1$ depending on its distance from the boundary, or allow $\delta_1$ to depend on the fixed point $x$.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 4.11 is false or ill-defined with its stated uniformity, and the main theorem's invocation requires a localized version.
issues.title: Max-min lemma cannot use one positive shift radius for every point of an open set
issues.why_classification: The convergence proof only needs shifts near a fixed interior contact point, so a standard localization repairs the lemma without changing the result.
